meta.title: Team AI Maturity Assessment
meta.subtitle: Answer a few questions to see how reusable, reviewable, and team-aware your AI-assisted work really is.

levels.name: Scattered
levels.description: Ad hoc AI use with isolated results. Context exists in individual chats and drives. No shared standards or reuse.
levels.tip: Focus on creating one shared context file and saving your best prompts.

levels.name: Structured
levels.description: Some repeatable practices but inconsistent. Context is scattered, handoffs vary, and reusable knowledge lives in individual tools.
levels.tip: Keep building foundations â standardize your handoffs and prompt library.

levels.name: Coordinated
levels.description: Aligned team practices and shared context. Your team works together with AI â the foundation is solid.
levels.tip: You're ready for governance and continuous improvement loops.

levels.name: Compounding
levels.description: Systematic advantage and continuous lift. AI is deeply embedded in your team's operating rhythm.
levels.tip: You're at the frontier â share what's working with peers.

Scattered.title: Create one shared team context file
Scattered.desc: Capture your mission, goals, audience, and key decisions your team's AI should always know.

Scattered.title: Save your 3 best prompts in a shared location
Scattered.desc: Pick prompts that have worked well and document them so others can use and improve them.

Scattered.title: Standardize one AI handoff template
Scattered.desc: Pick a simple, repeatable format so nothing gets lost between steps.

Structured.title: Formalize your prompt library with categories
Structured.desc: Group prompts by workflow or role so anyone can find what they need without asking.

Structured.title: Add a review step for AI-generated outputs
Structured.desc: Designate someone to spot-check and approve AI work before it becomes official.

Structured.title: Close your biggest context gap
Structured.desc: Pick the capability area that scored lowest and focus your next sprint there.

Coordinated.title: Build a staleness monitor for your context files
Coordinated.desc: Flag files that haven't been updated in 30+ days so your context stays current.

Coordinated.title: Create a governance checklist for AI workflows
Coordinated.desc: Document what good looks like so standards are maintained as the team grows.

Coordinated.title: Set up a continuous improvement loop
Coordinated.desc: Schedule a monthly review of what's working and what prompts need updating.

Compounding.title: Document your system for others to replicate
Compounding.desc: Your AI operating system is a competitive advantage â codify it so it scales.

Compounding.title: Mentor a peer team through their assessment
Compounding.desc: Teaching what works reinforces your own practices and builds your reputation.

Compounding.title: Explore context graph architecture
Compounding.desc: At this maturity level, queryable decision traces at scale become your next frontier.

sections.name: Shared Context
sections.desc: How well your team creates and maintains shared AI context.
questions: Our team has a shared document or file that describes our mission, goals, and key decisions that AI should always know.
When a new team member joins, they can quickly get AI tools up to speed on our work without asking everyone for context.
Team members use consistent background context when prompting AI tools â not whatever they happen to remember.
When our team's priorities or decisions change, we update our shared AI context files to reflect this.
Our AI context doesn't live in one person's head â it's documented and findable by anyone on the team.

sections.name: Prompt Reuse
sections.desc: How well your team creates, stores, and reuses high-value prompts.
questions: We have a shared prompt library where team members store and find reusable prompts.
High-value prompts are not trapped in private chats â they're saved somewhere the team can access.
Our prompts include expected inputs, outputs, and instructions so others can use them without guessing.
Prompts are grouped by workflow, role, or task so people can find what they need quickly.
We regularly reuse and adapt prompts that worked well instead of starting from scratch.

sections.name: Team Handoffs
sections.desc: How well context is preserved when work moves between people.
questions: When work moves from one team member to another, there's a standard format for summarizing AI context and decisions.
Handoff notes include what was tried, what worked, and what the AI needs to know to continue the work.
People don't have to re-explain the same background context every time they start a new conversation with AI.
Our handoff process captures key decisions and assumptions, not just task status.
When a project is paused and restarted, the team can quickly reload context without losing progress.

sections.name: Knowledge Capture
sections.desc: How consistently your team records decisions and domain knowledge.
questions: Valuable insights and decisions from AI-assisted work are captured somewhere durable â not just in chat history.
When the AI produces something exceptional, we document what prompt or approach led to that result.
Domain-specific knowledge (definitions, constraints, policies) is written down and accessible to AI tools.
We have a way to capture and tag decisions so they can be referenced later without asking the person who made them.
Knowledge doesn't disappear when someone leaves the team or goes on leave.

sections.name: Review & Governance
sections.desc: How your team reviews AI outputs and maintains standards.
questions: We have a clear process for reviewing AI-generated outputs before they become official or are acted upon.
There is someone or a role responsible for maintaining the quality of our AI context and prompts.
We track when context files or prompts were last updated and flag ones that may be stale.
Our team has shared standards for what makes a good prompt or AI output in our specific context.
When AI produces something wrong or misleading, we have a way to capture that feedback and improve.

sections.name: Workflow Integration
sections.desc: How deeply AI is integrated into your team's daily workflows.
questions: AI tools are consistently used across the team â not just by a few enthusiasts.
Our AI usage is integrated into regular workflows rather than used ad hoc when someone remembers.
We have standard places in our process where AI context is checked or updated (e.g., sprint start, handoffs).
Team members feel confident using AI tools because they know the context is reliable and up to date.
Our AI workflows have improved over time as we've learned what works and what doesn't.
